trial_name.text: Three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled monotherapy trials (Studies 1, 2, and 3), plus a fourth placebo-controlled add-on trial (Study 4)

citations.quote: The antihypertensive effectiveness of BYSTOLIC as monotherapy has been demonstrated in three randomized, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled trials at doses ranging from 1.25 to 40 mg for 12 weeks (Studies 1, 2, and 3). A fourth placebo-controlled trial demonstrated additional antihypertensive effects of BYSTOLIC at doses ranging from 5 to 20 mg when administered concomitantly with up to two other antihypertensive agents (ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, and thiazide diuretics) in patients with inadequate blood pressure control.

nct.text: Not stated in the reviewed documents

citations.quote: The antihypertensive effectiveness of BYSTOLIC as monotherapy has been demonstrated in three randomized, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled trials at doses ranging from 1.25 to 40 mg for 12 weeks (Studies 1, 2, and 3).

phase.text: Not specified by phase; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group dose-ranging studies

citations.quote: Three of these studies were placebo-controlled, parallel-group dose ranging studies. The fourth study was a dose ranging study on top of other antihypertensive treatments.

design.text: Randomized, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled, parallel-group dose-ranging trials; patients received BYSTOLIC or placebo once daily for twelve weeks

citations.quote: The antihypertensive effectiveness of BYSTOLIC as monotherapy has been demonstrated in three randomized, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled trials at doses ranging from 1.25 to 40 mg for 12 weeks (Studies 1, 2, and 3).
Patients received either BYSTOLIC or placebo once daily for twelve weeks.

population.text: Patients with mild to moderate hypertension with baseline diastolic blood pressures (DBP) of 95 to 109 mmHg; Study 3 enrolled only Black patients

citations.quote: The three monotherapy trials included a total of 2016 patients (1811 BYSTOLIC, 205 placebo) with mild to moderate hypertension who had baseline diastolic blood pressures (DBP) of 95 to 109 mmHg.
The third monotherapy trial (Study #3) studied 300 Black patients with a mean age of 51 years, 45% males, 14% diabetics, and 3% as PMs.

endpoint.text: Placebo-subtracted least-square mean reduction in trough sitting diastolic (and systolic) blood pressure

citations.quote: Table 1: LS mean placebo-subtracted effect for trough sitting diastolic blood pressure.

n.text: 2016 patients across the three monotherapy trials (1811 BYSTOLIC, 205 placebo); the add-on Study 4 enrolled 669 patients

citations.quote: The three monotherapy trials included a total of 2016 patients (1811 BYSTOLIC, 205 placebo) with mild to moderate hypertension who had baseline diastolic blood pressures (DBP) of 95 to 109 mmHg.
Study #4 enrolled 669 patients with a mean age of 54 years, 55% males, 54% Caucasians, 29% Blacks, 15% Hispanics, 1% Asians, 14% diabetics, and 5% PMs.

result.text: Statistically significant, generally dose-related placebo-subtracted least-square mean reductions in trough sitting systolic/diastolic BP; diastolic reductions by dose: Study 1 -5.1 (1.25 mg) to -8.3 mmHg (30-40 mg); Study 2 -3.2 to -4.5 mmHg; Study 3 (Black patients) -2.9 to -6.1 mmHg; Study 4 (add-on) -3.3 to -4.6 mmHg (* p<0.05 vs placebo)

citations.quote: * p<0.05 based on pair-wise comparison vs placebo

indication.text: BYSTOLIC is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

citations.quote: BYSTOLIC is indicated for the treatment of hypertension. BYSTOLIC may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents.

target_moa.text: Nebivolol is a beta-adrenergic receptor blocking agent that is preferentially beta-1 selective in extensive metabolizers at doses <=10 mg; the antihypertensive mechanism has not been definitively established but may involve decreased heart rate, decreased myocardial contractility, suppression of renin activity, and vasodilation

citations.quote: Nebivolol is a \beta-adrenergic receptor blocking agent. In extensive metabolizers (most of the population) and at doses less than or equal to 10 mg, nebivolol is preferentially \beta_1 selective.

The mechanism of action of the antihypertensive response of BYSTOLIC has not been definitively established. Possible factors that may be involved include: (1) decreased heart rate, (2) decreased myocardial contractility, (3) diminution of tonic sympathetic outflow to the periphery from cerebral vasomotor centers, (4) suppression of renin activity and (5) vasodilation and decreased peripheral vascu

modality.text: Small molecule (nebivolol, a racemic selective beta-1 receptor antagonist; new molecular entity)

citations.quote: Nebivolol, a racemic mixture of d- and l-isomers, is a selective \beta_1-receptor antagonist that has been developed for the treatment of ______ hypertension (proposed dosing range 2.5 – 10 mg; although some patients could potentially receive up to 20 mg twice daily off-label).
Nebivolol is a selective \beta_1 receptor antagonist and a new molecular entity.

key_safety.text: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (incidence >=1% and > placebo) included headache (9% at 5 mg vs 6% placebo), fatigue (up to 5% at 20-40 mg vs 1% placebo), dizziness (up to 4% vs 2% placebo), diarrhea, and nausea; the most common signs of overdose were bradycardia and hypotension

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)(1)) for nebivolol, a new molecular entity selective beta-1 blocker, for hypertension; the application originally submitted April 30, 2004 received an Approvable action in 2005 over mouse Leydig cell tumors, and was approved December 17, 2007 after a complete response, without referral to an advisory committee.

Nebivolol is a selective \beta_1 receptor antagonist and a new molecular entity.
On May 31, 2005, NDA 21-742 for Nevibolol Tablets received an “Approvable” action. The “Approvable” deficiency was:

NDA 21-742 was not referred to an advisory committee for review because there are several previously approved agents in the \beta-blocker class of drugs, evaluation of the safety data did not reveal particular safety issues that were unexpected for this class, and the design and results of the efficacy trials did not pose particular concerns.
